tasks.short: Test geological specimens with precision instruments

steps.what: Test diamonds, abrasives, soil or rocks and determine geological characteristics

tasks.design: Retain specimen preparation, instrument use and geological interpretation. The {OTHER} laboratory instrument software may already capture readings, but its runtime earns no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical specimen handling and appropriate testing require specialist judgment.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional verified replacement is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising preparation artefacts and invalid readings.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the observed characteristics support a geological conclusion.
tasks.altitude: Hands-on testing and interpretation remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Distinguish specimen variation from preparation error

evidence.claim: Instrument data capture does not itself replace physical specimen testing and interpretation.

assumptions: Boundary covers specimen testing and direct interpretation, excluding later report assembly.
Geoscientist verifies specimen identity, calibration, preparation and readings during s1; no structured valid-result flag is assumed.
OTHER means laboratory instrument software. Test native instrument functions before new systems; no new change is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no software or process is added.
research_questions: Which invalid readings can only be recognised from preparation and specimen context?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives zero gross and net; optical and chemical testing retain physical work and scientific judgment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine ways to mitigate mineral dust dispersion from site evidence and constraints

tasks.design: Keep site-specific mitigation judgment with the geoscientist using the evidence in {DOCS}. No automatic recommendation or invented report-writing baseline is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Effective mitigation depends on source behaviour, exposure pathways and operational constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: General text generation does not establish site-specific mitigation effectiveness.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing controls that work under changing site conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Identify missing evidence and distinguish plausible controls from justified recommendations.
tasks.altitude: Mitigation judgment and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Connect source control with observed exposure pathways

evidence.claim: The supplied evidence does not demonstrate replacement of site-specific mineral dust mitigation judgment.

assumptions: Boundary is selecting mitigation options; sampling, engineering implementation and control verification are separate existing work.
Field teams produce observations and the geoscientist evaluates their adequacy during s1; no precomputed control effectiveness or safe-exposure flag is assumed.
Test existing document and analysis tools before additions; no tool change is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no new process or system is introduced.
unknowns: Dust composition, site conditions and control performance evidence
research_questions: What evidence is missing before mitigation options can be justified?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives zero gross and net. Both familiar sites and unusual dust compositions retain evidence-based mitigation judgment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define research questions and collect geomechanical and geochemical literature records
Screen abstracts for relevance to the specified sequestration processes

loop.purpose: Prioritise abstracts while the scientist decides relevance
loop.input: Search export, criteria and scientist labels
loop.check: Scientist verifies relevance against criteria, known relevant papers and a held-out sample of low-ranked records
loop.stop: Fixed screening budget with no automatic exclusions; missed known papers or unstable ranking returns the set to manual screening
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters cannot reliably identify varied descriptions of the relevant geological process

steps.what: Research geomechanical and geochemical processes through critical reading and scientific investigation

tasks.design: Use native deduplication and filters in the {OTHER} literature screening software first, then bounded relevance ranking. Full reading, experiments, scientific interpretation and conclusions remain with the geoscientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searching relevant literature leaves many abstracts to inspect.
tasks.enabler_now: Human-labelled relevance ranking can reorder the screening queue.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing whether results transfer to the proposed sequestration conditions.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less abstract screening while substantive research remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Check screening recall independently of ranking confidence

evidence.claim: ASReview LAB reorders abstracts while a person screens.
The proposed effort split and carbon sequestration screening savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary includes literature discovery and substantive process research; it excludes implementing a storage project.

Geoscientist produces query, inclusion criteria, source ids, titles, abstracts, publication versions and known relevant examples in s1. Initial relevance labels and further labels are captured by the scientist within s2 retained time. Missing abstracts or identifiers receive manual screening.
OTHER means literature screening and research software. Native catalogue filters and deduplication precede model ranking.
No automatic research conclusion, reference generation or completeness claim is made.
research_questions: Can ranking reduce screening effort while retaining known relevant and independently sampled studies?

already_counted.description: Labels, relevance checks and recall sample

incremental.description: Maintain screening settings and inspect missed records

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94 gives6 gross minus3 upkeep=3 net. Small searches may remain manual; large relevant record sets may yield1% of total research time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Research ways to reduce megacity ecological footprints

steps.what: Define megacity scenarios, evidence and ecological footprint comparison assumptions
Calculate and compare ecological footprint scenarios using the selected method
Research mechanisms, interpret comparisons and identify credible ecological footprint reductions

tasks.design: Configure parameterised comparisons in the {OTHER} environmental modelling software. The scientist defines system boundaries and evaluates mechanisms, rebound effects and whether proposed reductions are credible.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated scenario entry and output assembly interrupt substantive research.
tasks.enabler_now: Parameterised models can rerun specified scenarios and refresh output tables.
tasks.still_hard: Comparing cities fairly and avoiding displacement of impacts beyond the boundary.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful boundaries and assess causal claims.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated scenario operation while research questions and conclusions stay human.

reach.learn: Interpret boundary choices and sensitivity results

evidence.claim: SimaPro supports parameterised life cycle models and refreshing report tables; this supports scenario mechanics, not comprehensive megacity research conclusions.
The proposed urban research effort and savings are unmeasured and apply only where repeated scenario work exists.

assumptions: Boundary is comparative research, excluding planning decisions and physical implementation. Use this design only for research with an established repeated quantitative scenario component.

Geoscientist produces source/version, population and activity quantities, units, functional boundary, time period, factors, uncertainty and scenario parameter sets in s1. Evidence gathering and structured capture retain all s1 time; missing data require manual investigation, never guessed factors.
OTHER means environmental modelling software. Test native parameterisation and report refresh before custom code; existing solver runtime earns no saving.
Savings apply to manual scenario operation and output assembly, not scientific investigation or interpretation.
unknowns: Whether this research uses repeated scenarios and has compatible data
research_questions: Does parameterisation reduce repeated operation while preserving boundary and sensitivity transparency?

incremental.description: Maintain scenarios, factors and reproducibility checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R70 gives30 gross minus8 upkeep=22 net. Qualitative studies or existing parameterisation yield zero; repeated manual scenario comparisons may yield5%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Testing and mitigation judgment remain human; literature prioritisation and repeat scenario operations gain bounded support.
reach: Discuss model boundaries with urban planners and environmental scientists
role.ambitious_version: A geoscientist who can trace research conclusions to evidence, assumptions and reproducible comparisons.
